terra.problem: The claim that crowds appear throughout the Gospels reaches outside the passage and has no reference.
Calling the question sneaky and comparing it to a cookie jokes about the card’s question.
The verse says the sheep follow Jesus; it does not say that walking with Him comes first.
The passage does not say that nobody bows in the scene. It says the Jews pick up stones.
Papa refers to the card and comments on how its statement was presented.
Identifying Moses as Israel’s leader is a fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
Saying they were upset assigns them a feeling the text does not state, without marking it as Papa’s guess.
Identifying David as Israel’s king is a fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The explanation repeats the same fact about John and ends with a generic observation about names.
John 1:40–42 does not establish that Peter was one of Jesus’ disciples, so the reference does not support that identification.
The cookie comparison does not make a clear parallel: a batch of cookies being reliable is not the same action as someone’s words being true.
The passage does not say that nobody across the Jordan tells Jesus to leave. It says many come to Him and many believe.
